title: How to write a great story
examples: How do I make my characters feel real?
What makes a good story setting?
Can you give me an example of showing instead of telling?

explain.say: Today we learn how to write a great story.

draw.text: How to write a great story
Story Elements: Character, Setting, Problem, Solution

explain.say: First we need a character who does things.

draw.text: Character: Who is the story about?

explain.say: Next we need a setting where the story happens.

draw.text: Setting: Where and when does it happen?

explain.say: Every story needs a problem that must be solved.

draw.text: Problem: The conflict that drives the story

explain.say: The solution is how the character fixes the problem.
Show don't tell means using actions instead of words.

draw.text: Show vs Tell: Actions over words

faq.q: What is the difference between problem and solution?
faq.a: The problem is the main difficulty in the story. The solution is the action that resolves that difficulty.
asks: How do I end the story?

faq.q: Do I need a character, setting, problem, and solution?
faq.a: These are the main building blocks of most stories. Having them makes your writing much stronger.
asks: What if I skip one part?

faq.q: What does 'show don't tell' really mean?
faq.a: It means showing the reader what is happening using details. Instead of saying it, you let them see it happen.
asks: Can you give me another example of showing?

faq.q: Is the setting just where the story happens?
faq.a: The setting is more than just a place. It can include the time period and the atmosphere too.
asks: Does the setting affect the story?

faq.q: How long should the problem be?
faq.a: The problem should be big enough to keep the reader interested. It needs enough time to build up to the solution.
asks: How much time do I spend on the problem?

facts: A character is the person or animal in the story.
The setting tells the reader where and when the story takes place.
The problem creates the tension that keeps the reader reading.
Showing uses action and description rather than just stating a feeling.

quiz.say: The main difficulty that the character must overcome is called the:
quiz.why: The problem is the central challenge that drives the plot forward.

wrong.1: A character is a person, not the challenge itself.
wrong.2: The setting is the place, not the difficulty.
wrong.3: The solution is what happens after the problem.

quiz.say: Which sentence shows anger using action?
quiz.why: This uses physical action to let the reader feel the anger.

wrong.0: This is too abstract and does not use concrete actions.
wrong.2: This only tells the reader the emotion without showing it.
wrong.3: Yelling is an action, but 'clenched fists' is a more contained physical sign.

quiz.say: If a story is set in a jungle, what element is the jungle itself?
quiz.why: The jungle provides the time and place for the story to happen.

wrong.0: The jungle is a place, not a person.
wrong.1: The jungle might cause a problem, but it is not the problem itself.
wrong.2: The solution is the answer, not the location.
